course.title: AP World History: Modern
course.description: Understand the people, ideas, and connections that shaped the world from c. 1200 to the present.
course.previewDescription: Explore how states rose, belief systems spread, trade networks connected regions, and revolutions reshaped societies from c. 1200 to the present.

unit.title: Global Conflict
unit.description: Study how empires collapsed, why two world wars were fought and how they were conducted, how the Depression reshaped economies, and how mass atrocities happened.

themes.title: Interactions of humans with the environment

themes.title: Political systems and governance

themes.title: Economic systems

themes.title: Cultural developments and interactions

questions.prompt: The collapse of the Qing and Ottoman empires was similar in that both
choices: led to the restoration of absolute monarchies

questions.prompt: Which claim about revolutions after 1900 is most defensible?
choices: They promised land and social change but produced unstable aftermaths
They ended inequality immediately in every country where they took place
They restored traditional monarchies
They were led by foreign colonial powers
questions.explanation: Russia and Mexico both faced long conflict after revolution.
choiceExplanations: Russia and Mexico both faced long conflict after revolution.
They were led by local movements.
questions.distinguisher: Civil wars and uneven reforms show that inequality did not end at once.

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, the Bolsheviks won support by promising
choices: land, bread, and an end to the war
a return of the tsar to power
a stronger effort to win the war
land and bread through victory in the war
questions.explanation: Their slogans promised land, bread, and an end to the senseless war.
choiceExplanations: Their slogans promised land, bread, and an end to the senseless war.
They called for ending the war.

questions.distinguisher: The Bolsheviks promised to end the war, not to win it.

stimulusBlocks.attribution: John Reed, American journalist and socialist who witnessed the Russian Revolution in Petrograd, Ten Days That Shook the World, 1919
stimulusBlocks.citation: John Reed, Ten Days That Shook the World (1919), ch. 1. Project Gutenberg eBook #3076.
stimulusBlocks.note: The Bolsheviki were the Bolsheviks, led by Lenin. Soviets were councils of workers and soldiers. The Provisional Government ruled Russia between the tsar's abdication in March 1917 and the Bolshevik seizure of power in November 1917. The ellipsis after “treachery” appears in Reed's own text.
stimulusBlocks.text:
In this atmosphere of corruption, of monstrous half-truths, one clear note sounded day after day, the deepening chorus of the Bolsheviki, "All Power to the Soviets! All power to the direct representatives of millions on millions of common workers, soldiers, peasants. Land, bread, an end to the senseless war, an end to secret diplomacy, speculation, treachery. . . . The Revolution is in danger, and with it the cause of the people all over the world!" . . .

Week by week food became scarcer. The daily allowance of bread fell from a pound and a half to a pound, then three quarters, half, and a quarter-pound. Toward the end there was a week without any bread at all.

questions.prompt: Reed's description of the Bolsheviks is most likely shaped by
choices: his service as an official of the tsar
his opposition to all revolutions
his role as a Bolshevik commander in the Russian civil war
his sympathy as an American socialist for their cause
questions.explanation: Reed was a socialist who admired the revolution, which shapes his favorable tone.
choiceExplanations: Reed was a socialist who admired the revolution, which shapes his favorable tone.
questions.distinguisher: Reed was a journalist and sympathizer, not a military commander.

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, many Chinese blamed the Qing for
choices: succeeding in the Boxer Rebellion
failing to defend China against foreign powers
defeating Japan in 1895
creating the Republic of China
questions.explanation: Defeats by Japan and foreign armies discredited the Qing.
choiceExplanations: Defeats by Japan and foreign armies discredited the Qing.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 7.1 key concept: states around the world challenged the existing political and social order, including the collapse of the Qing, Ottoman, and Russian empires
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing the fall of the Qing dynasty, 1898–1912
stimulusBlocks.text:
After defeats by Japan in 1895 and by foreign armies during the Boxer Rebellion of 1899 to 1901, many Chinese blamed the Qing for failing to defend the country. Revolutionaries led by Sun Yat-sen called for nationalism, democracy, and the people's livelihood. An army uprising in 1911 spread quickly, and the last emperor abdicated in 1912.

The new Republic of China was weak. Regional military leaders known as warlords controlled much of the country, and the nation would not be fully unified again for decades.

choices: a smooth transition to a strong republic
the restoration of the Qing
the immediate unification of China
instability that continued after the revolution
questions.explanation: Warlords controlled much of the country after 1912.
choiceExplanations: Warlords controlled much of the country after 1912.
questions.distinguisher: Warlords divided China, so unification did not come quickly.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, Emiliano Zapata demanded
choices: land for peasants
the return of Díaz
more foreign investment
rule by a king

choiceExplanations: Zapata's slogan was Land and Liberty.
questions.distinguisher: Díaz welcomed foreign investment; Zapata wanted land.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 7.1 key concept: the Mexican Revolution challenged the existing political and social order
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing the Mexican Revolution, 1910–1920
stimulusBlocks.text:
Porfirio Díaz ruled Mexico for more than thirty years, welcoming foreign investment while a small elite owned most of the land. In 1910 a revolt against him began, and Díaz fled in 1911. Leaders such as Emiliano Zapata demanded land for peasants under the slogan “Land and Liberty.”

The fighting lasted a decade and killed perhaps a million people. The Constitution of 1917 promised land reform, workers' rights, and national ownership of mineral resources, though many of its promises were carried out only later.

questions.prompt: The Mexican and Russian revolutions were similar in that both
choices: were caused by the Great Depression
promised land to foreign investors
promised land to peasants
restored monarchies
questions.explanation: Both drew support with promises of land.
choiceExplanations: Both drew support with promises of land.
questions.distinguisher: Both promised land to peasants, not to foreign investors.

choices: the spread of fascism from Europe

questions.prompt: Which demand is part of the Bolshevik slogan quoted in the passage?
choices: A return to rule by the tsar
Unrestricted private trade in grain
Land, bread, and an end to the senseless war
Allied military support for the government
questions.explanation: The slogan calls for land, bread, and an end to the war, along with power for the soviets.
choiceExplanations: The Bolsheviks opposed the old tsarist order.

The slogan calls for land, bread, and an end to the war, along with power for the soviets.
The Bolsheviks wanted an end to the war.
questions.distinguisher: Bread was scarce, but the slogan did not call for private grain markets.

questions.prompt: Which event had occurred before the situation Reed describes?
choices: The Treaty of Brest-Litovsk with Germany in 1918
The tsar's abdication in March 1917
The Allied intervention in the Russian Civil War
The founding of the Soviet Union in December 1922
questions.explanation: Reed describes Bolshevik agitation against the Provisional Government, which had formed after the tsar abdicated.
choiceExplanations: The treaty ending Russia's war with Germany came in March 1918, after the Bolsheviks took power.
Reed describes Bolshevik agitation against the Provisional Government, which had formed after the tsar abdicated.
Allied intervention in the civil war followed the Bolshevik seizure of power.
The Soviet Union was formed in 1922.
questions.distinguisher: The Treaty of Brest-Litovsk responded to the Bolshevik demand for peace, so it came after, not before, the scene Reed describes.
